newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli forces close two PA security offices.
newsitem.headline: Israeli forces close two PA security offices.

text.p: The Israeli army stormed two Palestinian Authority security offices in the West Bank and closed them down on Tuesday, an Authority official said.
Jibril Rajoub, Preventive Security chief in the West Bank, told Reuters: "The Israeli army stormed into two of my offices in Hableh and Bidya villages in the West Bank and shut them down."
The West Bank villages are still under ultimate Israeli security control, but public order responsibilities were transferred to the Authority last year.
The army said the offices were not allowed in the area under an interim Israeli-Palestinian peace deal.
"The Israeli move is one form of blackmail. We will not submit nor raise the white flag in any way," Rajoub said.

Another Palestinian security official said: "The Israelis are angry at Rajoub and other PLO security chiefs for halting security coordination with Israel and they are trying to provoke them to resume contacts."

The Authority halted security cooperation with Israel in response to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's decision to suspend political contacts with it, retaining contact only on security, after a Moslem militant bombed a Tel Aviv cafe on March 21, killing three Israelis.
PLO-Israel relations deteriorated and peace talks were suspended after Israel began a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on March 18.
